title: Adic constructible complexes and stratified perfect local models
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning that it admits a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring with a unique maximal ideal $I$ and residue field $A/I$, and assume $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $\widehat A_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/I^n)_X$, where the terms are constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Use categories of module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived extension of scalars [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(\widehat A_X))$, the following conditions are equivalent.

(a) $K$ is locally derived $I\widehat A_X$-complete [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete], and $K\otimes^L_{\widehat A_X}(A/I)_X\simeq\nu_X^*C$ for some bounded étale $A/I$-complex $C$ with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude. Here constructible means that each cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finitely presented $A/I$-module values [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] on a finite constructible locally closed stratification; finite Tor amplitude means that some integers $a\leq b$ satisfy $H^q(C\otimes^L_{(A/I)_X}N)=0$ for every étale $(A/I)_X$-module sheaf $N$ in degree zero and $q\notin[a,b]$.

(b) There is a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] $X=\coprod_\alpha S_\alpha$ by constructible locally closed subschemes such that, on a pro-étale cover of each $S_\alpha$, $K|_{S_\alpha}$ is isomorphic to $\widehat A_{S_\alpha}\otimes_A P^\bullet$ for a perfect $A$-complex $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], represented by a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules. The coefficient restriction is identified with $\widehat A_{S_\alpha}=\varprojlim_n(A/I^n)_{S_\alpha}$; the tensor expression means termwise extension of the constant complex $P^\bullet$.

Every complex satisfying these equivalent conditions is bounded in cohomology. These complexes form a full triangulated subcategory: it contains zero, is invariant under isomorphisms and integer shifts, and whenever two vertices of a distinguished triangle satisfy (a), so does the third. No finite dimension hypothesis on $X$ and no invertibility of residue characteristics on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.8(1),(2), Remark 6.5.10, and Proposition 6.6.11, reverse implication; proetale.tex Tag 099L (section-derived-completion-noetherian) and Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion).

proof.text: Every $k$-module sheaf is flat. A bounded étale $k$-complex with cohomology in $[a,b]$ is quasi-isomorphic, by its canonical truncations, to a complex with terms in $[a,b]$; this complex has flat terms, so it is K-flat and its tensor with a degree-zero sheaf computes derived tensor. That tensor commutes with cohomology, so the complex has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$.

Assume (a). Refine the strata for the finitely many nonzero $H^q(C)$ by their actual fibre-product intersections. The finite-stratification pullback lemma retains their local constant finite module values. Each stratum is Noetherian: locally it is a quotient of a Noetherian affine chart, and its underlying subspace is quasi-compact. Step 1 restricts completeness; comparison-pullback identifies the residue with $\nu_S^*(C|_S)$. Step 2 gives finite Tor amplitude there. The residue-lisse perfect-lifting lemma now supplies the covers and perfect $A$-complexes required by (b).

Assume (b). The perfect-model lemma gives completeness, constant finite-dimensional residue cohomology and finite cohomological bounds on every model cover. Step 1 detects completeness globally. Apply stratified-local bounds to $K$ and to its residue reduction separately. Both are bounded globally; this also proves the claimed boundedness for every object satisfying (a).

By the perfect-model lemma and the exact restrictions along stratum immersions and to slices, which commute with cohomology sheaves, each residue cohomology sheaf is locally constant with finitely presented values on the given strata. Global constructibility agrees with affine-local constructibility on both sites. As $X$ is qcqs and $k$ is discrete Noetherian, constructible comparison gives a bounded étale complex $C$ realizing this residue. Its finite-type cohomology values are finitely presented over $k$, and global constructibility supplies the finite strata of (a). Step 2 supplies finite Tor amplitude. Together with step 4 this proves (a).

The complete locus is triangulated by the ringed-completion lemma. The discrete Noetherian constructible weak Serre lemma and the bounded weak-Serre cohomology theorem make bounded intrinsically constructible residue complexes triangulated. Global constructibility and comparison identify this residue condition with bounded constructible étale origin. Step 2 adds finite Tor amplitude automatically. Residue reduction is exact, so the intersection of its inverse image with the complete locus has zero, isomorphism invariance, all shifts and two-out-of-three in every ambient triangle, as asserted.
